english: Tristan was the greatest hero of the Brotherhood of Wardens during Patria's Third Rebellion. He was so instrumental to their cause that the Wardens constructed a ritual to preserve him in case of future need. In the centuries since, Tristan has been called when the Wardens are at their greatest need. Each time Tristan appears exactly as he was when the ritual was first performed. He has no memory of any of his prior manifestations, and doesn't bear any evidence of injuries from those events. Even deaths during manifestations don't keep him from being summoned again. [PARAGRAPH]This is because Tristan is actually held suspended in the Isle of Birds. The ritual creates a duplicate manifestation of him each time. Summoned manifestations have a limited duration. No one remembers that they aren't summoning the real Tristan, or realizes that they could summon multiple copies to fulfill different missions for different factions. [PARAGRAPH]Tristan always appears with living ivory armor with gemellus engraving as well as a palladium torc. [PARAGRAPH] (Living Ivory is a divine metal with an affinity to the Life dominion. It perfectly repairs itself, as well as helping its bearers heal faster. Gemellus is a rose colored metal with an affinity to the Spirit dominion. All gamellus ore originating in a single vein maintains an eternal empathic bond to all the other gamellus ore from that same vein. This makes it the preferred material for wedding bands, as it allows a couple to always sense their spouse's presence and emotional state. Palladium has an affinity for force dominion and is frequently used in binding circles or circlets to enforce oaths. )[PARAGRAPH]Tristan also carries a gemellus ring, called the [LINK=PROMTOION_DAHLIA_BAND]Dahlia Band[\\LINK]. The Dahlia Band maintains the connection with the real Tristan and strengthens the manifestation. In rare cases the manifestation has given the Dahlia Band to another. If the Dahlia band is given away it remains after the manifestation is gone. It is a sacred symbol of the brotherhood. It would remain with the one who it was given to, never gifted to another, until it was buried with them. It is a connection to Tristan, for whatever that bond might grant them.

[ICON_BULLET]The true Tristan remains in the Isle of Birds and can never be resurrected, but [LINK=UNIT_TRISTAN]duplicate manifestations[\\LINK] can be summoned through a ritual performed in [LINK=PROMOTION_BROTHERHOOD_OF_WARDENS]Brotherhood of Wardens[\\LINK] cities or by a Brotherhood unit that carries his [LINK=PROMTOION_DAHLIA_BAND]Dahlia Band[\\LINK].

Velgyr is very autistic dwarf and shuns people, preferring instead to dwell in a world of his own creations. He retreated deep into a mountain where he lived alone, creating a city full of enchanted inhabitants. From stone citizens that were nearly perfect imitations of the living, to tiny enchanted butterflies, and everything in between. This foul breed of wolf has adapted to using the disease it carries like a venom that can take out whole armies and villages.
Kezef

Kezef was the Imprimatur Council member whose experiments killed all the animals on the Grigi plains. Kezef mastered the art of being able to stitch various creatures together. He created the first flesh golems and chimera, and collaborated with students of Leucetios to produce many hybrid races. His biggest feats were reserved for his own body, grafting himself into the form of a living giant.
Mikel Dylantyr

There is an ocean of fire that dwells within Mikel Dylantyr. Although this Imprimatur Council member could channel it, his true power was tied to his rage. When enraged, fire flowed out of him hot enough to melt stone and waves of lava flow from him. An entire city stood once where there is now only ash and rippled stone.
Greysun

Greysun rode on the storm. This Imprimatur Council member could become air or lightning at will, dance at the center of the tornado and slip unseen through the mist. He slept upon cloudbanks and woke up in new countries. He was deathly claustrophobic and had a hard time being inside any building.
Badb

There is a blizzard that rages across Erebus, horrible, sudden and dark. It settles into an area at night, and is always gone by dawn. Those lost in the blizzard sometimes find an ancient castle that didn't exist before and seek shelter from the cold. The castle is haunted, endlessly reliving one horrific night. But the king is very much alive, Badb is caught in this nightmare and is as powerful as he is insane.
Leucetios

The mother of nations is eternally young, and always pregnant, giving birth every 9 months, usually to twins or triplets. Each of her children are heroes in their own right and they all share a bond with their mother that they can draw strength, healing and support from her.
Laroth

Laroth's incredible gift is to inspire sacrifice in others. Those he speaks to will give their life savings, or even their lives to him. They seek to subjugate themselves to any cause he offers. In life this giving was finite, but when Laroth's entered the underworld he found this sacrifice to be infinite, and began raising an army of worshiping souls that served him alone. He would create his own empire in the underworld, and come very close to becoming the God of Death.
Jenkin

Jenkin is not human, he is a race created to guard a labyrinth between the worlds. He is immune to time, but not immortal. His form is covered in runes he has inscribed, making him nearly invulnerable, as strong as a giant, allowing him to pass through stone, dirt and metal, keeping him from requiring air or sleep, and allowing him to sense anything that is touching the earth within miles of his location. [PARAGRAPH:2]The story starts on another plane. This is a world full of spirits and a race of men called the Souman that practice runecrafting, a type of magic where magic is bound into longstanding symbols. It wasn't as flashy as the magic of Erebus, but it was powerful. [PARAGRAPH]This world was small, warm and abundant with fresh water and food. War was almost unknown. [PARAGRAPH]Occasionally one of the Souman would be born with a rare gift, the ability to see the spirits that inhabited the world. One day a young boy with this gift disappeared form the highland village he belonged to. A week later he was found being tended to by spirits outside of tower only those with the gift to see spirits could see. One of the Soulen's hero's, a man named Kiras Tor, also had the gift and went to investigate the tower. Inside he found 8 archways. He used a rune to open one, entered and he dropped dead. He lay dead for a few moments until his eyes fluttered open and he took a breath. He told stories of awakening on a funeral stone as another man, a man who lived underground, who called himself one of the Khazad. Kiras said he lived for 8 years among the Khazad, in a world full of wonders the Soulen had never imagined. And horrors beyond anything in their world. [PARAGRAPH]Kiras and the elders were worried that one of these horrors could find its way into their world so they declared the area off limits and so it stayed for two hundred years. [PARAGRAPH]Until the Jorgano came. These were beasts made for war, and they were totally immune to magic. They set immediately to purging the world of the Soulen. And the Soulen had no way to stand against them. [PARAGRAPH]Remembering the tower, the elders sent their most talented runecaster, Pheden Mara, through another archway. They were hopeful she could find a way to stop the Jorgano. Just as Kiras had, Pheden dropped dead. [PARAGRAPH]Long minutes went by and then another waiting at the tower with the gift to see spirits saw a woman walk through a different archway. She didn't look like Pheden and her body rapidly decomposed and turned to dust. Pheden's spirit arose from the body and traced a rune in the air before being swept off to the afterlife. [PARAGRAPH]Then 50 naked warriors came marching out of the archway the body had come out of. These were perfectly formed men, made for battle. They had stood guard of another world, called the Nexus since their world was formed. They knew the Jorgano and hated them. And Pheden had convinced them to come to her world and help in the battle. [PARAGRAPH]These were the Myrikhan, ageless, unsleeping sentries of the Nexus. And they were able to stall the Jorgano defense, but the Jorgano were to many. [PARAGRAPH]More help was needed. So the elders decided to send another through the tower. A Soulen named Ran who saw Pheden's spirit (none understood the rune she had made), and a Myrikhan guard named Jenkin to watch over him. [PARAGRAPH]Ran opened the portal and he and Jenkin went through. [PARAGRAPH]The tale of Ran and Jenkin's travels is to long to tell here. This was an entire DnD campaign. They found traces of Pheden's and Kiras's travels (though Kiras's were ancient legends). And discovered that Pheden's rune showed the passage of time relative to the Soulen home world. Most worlds were so much slower than the the Soulen home world that Ran and Jenkin sould stay there for years with only a few seconds going by. [PARAGRAPH]In each world Jenkin could pass through the archway directly, as long as Ran opened it. He couldn't take anything through, which is why he was naked each time. Ran's body didn't go through but his spirit did, and he would possess an empty vessel on the other side if one was available (some worlds were simply blocked because no vessel was available). If Ran died on a world his spirit was swept back through the soul gate (which they came to call the tower) and that world was forever closed to him). Each world had a tower with 8 archways and they went to a wide variety of places. [PARAGRAPH]In his travels Ran inhabited a flesh golem created by an incompetent witch doctor (who was thrilled to find his creation had finally come to life), an assassin guild leader who had just been poisoned (the player had to save or die from the poison again), a mages clone, a well perserved lich where the player and a lich had to vie for control of the body with the player being more powerful during the day and the lich being more powerful at night, and many more. [PARAGRAPH]A devil followed Ran through a few worlds, offering some measure of power to help save the Ran's world in exchange for his soul. Ran refused the deal, not trusting it would be enough to save his world (and not wanting to spend his afterlife in hell). [PARAGRAPH]Then Jenkin failed at his guard duties. Ran was in the body of an Assassin Guild leader. A rival guild had poisoned him, and apparently that hadn't worked (since he was apparently still alive). The rival guild planned an attack and Jenkin rushed to the site of the attack (the front of the guild) and left Ran alone in his bed chamber. [PARAGRAPH]Unfortunately the attack was just a ruse to draw the guards away from their leader. The real attack happened when the rival guild members slipped into the guild leaders bed chamber. Ran was outnumbered and had no way to defend himself. The devil returned, offering to save Ran in exchange for his soul. [PARAGRAPH]Ran agreed. [PARAGRAPH]The devil did save him, Ran survived the attack and blamed Jenkin for failing to guard him. Jenkin was crushed at the sacrifice his friend had to make, but understood that he had done it to continue his quest to try and save his people. [PARAGRAPH]Unfortunately it wasn't the first failure. Ran died again, torn apart in a maelstrom of another world. But before his spirit could return to the soul gate the devil plucked it from the ether and delivered it to hell. [PARAGRAPH]Without anyone who could see (let alone open the archway in the tower) Jenkin was stranded on the last world they were on. He spent long years as a hermit, cursing himself for failing at his task before hearing of the rise of magic in the world's empire. He sought out the Archmage and King of the world and asked to train. King Kylorin found he had an affinity for Earth magic and trained him to use it. Jenkin served as a guard to Kylorin for years. Jenkin attempted to get Kylorin to help him return through the soul gate but Kylorin became less interested over time. When Jenkin told Laroth about the soul gate Laroth disappeared. [PARAGRAPH]Kylorin started becoming more cruel so Jenkin slipped away, returning to his life as a hermit. Ages passed, the Age of Magic ended and the Age of Ice came and passed. [PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Rebirth the goddess Ceridwen found Ran being tortured within the mires of hell. She lifted him out of his anguish and offered him a deal. He was once willing to trade his immortal soul to save a world, now she asked if he would trade an entire world to save his immortal soul. [PARAGRAPH]Ran agreed and she had him reborn in Erebus as Tebryn Arbandi. [PARAGRAPH]Tebryn's story is also to long for this entry. But the short version is he formed the Deadlands and the Black tower and attempted to cause Armageddon. He was stopped by a heroic party of adventurers after a long campaign. These heroes were helped during their darkest hours by a shadowy figure that knew of everything that sat upon or under the earth. This was Jenkin. [PARAGRAPH]Inside the Black Tower the party got close to Tebryn. Tebryn knew someone powerful had been working against him for months. But realized who it was as the party got close. He called out to Jenkin, who answered his call. [PARAGRAPH]The two argued, Tebryn blaming everything that happened on Jenkin and telling him about the torments he had endured by sacrificing himself. And that he had suffered enough for any man and wouldn't do it any longer, if if the world had to be destroyed to stop it. Jenkin only asked for forgiveness, but said he could not allow Tebryn to continue on the path he was on. [PARAGRAPH]Tebryn killed him, Jenkin didn't stop him. [PARAGRAPH]After seeing their benefactor struck down the party charged in and after a heroic fight they beat him.

Casswallawn is a Patrian title that means "wielder of blue flame. " This flame is no ordinary fire, but the form that Gastrius took once his body was broken by the Coven of the Black Candle. Gastrius can no longer interact with Creation directly except through a willing host, whom he can advice and empower but not control. If his host dies, but Blue Flames may pass to a mage who slew him or return to the Cave of the Ancestors to await a more worthy vessel.
Apophis the Endless Hunger

Apophis began as a Father or Worlds, one of the Seven Aspects of Amathaon. These True Angels traveled out from the heart of creation and made infinite new lands as they passed. Though the raw form already existed, it was the Father of Worlds that turned the continents, oceans, mountains, etc., into living worlds complete with unique and wonderful creations. [PARAGRAPH]During the Godswar, Agares corrupted each of the Father of Worlds and turned them into the Unraveling. They lost all their Creation affinity and became Dark creatures said to be able to destroy creation. [PARAGRAPH]As one of the Unraveling, Apophis took the form of great snake capable of swallowing lakes, mountains or stars. Anything he swallowed wss lost forever, including many angels, dragons and giants during the Godswar. [PARAGRAPH]Agares bound each of the Unraveling at the forging of the Compact. He transformed Apophis into an ordinary seeming goat, and set him free to roam in Creation in this humble form. He has wandered widely but spends most of his time in the Balseraph lands. He occasionally joins adventuring parties, causing trouble, kneecapping ogres and eating everything in sight. He tends to favor adventurers who are drunks, liars and thieves. There is a statue of him in Jubilee, built after he chased away a pyromancer that was threatening the city. He traveled for a while with Maros the Umberguard and saved Maros's life on more than one occasion. [PARAGRAPH]In either form, Apophis is largely immune to mind, body and spirit magic. He is nearly indestructible and attempting to transform him will draw the attention of wraiths. He can also destroy most magical items by devouring them. [PARAGRAPH]Transformation, especially one that doesn't erode over time, is well outside of the entropy dominion; Agares used a bone circlet to maintain the spell. He couldn't keep the circlet close to him, or his own presence would destroy, it so he cast it into the Black Sea in the razor-glass plains of Naraka (in the lowest level of hell where demons go to drink and forget their lives and become wraiths). [PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Ruin Belphegor shall send Paymon Hora to the Black Sea to reclaim the bone circlet, but she shall be overcome by the Wraiths that surround the lake and dragged into the depths herself.
Abaddon, Lord of Locusts

Abaddon began as a Father or Worlds, one of the Seven Aspects of Amathaon. These True Angels traveled out from the heart of creation and made infinite new lands as they passed. Though the raw form already existed, it was the Father of Worlds that turned the continents, oceans, mountains, etc., into living worlds complete with unique and wonderful creations. [PARAGRAPH]During the Godswar, Agares corrupted each of the Father of Worlds and turned them into the Unraveling. They lost all their Creation affinity and became Dark creatures said to be able to destroy creation. [PARAGRAPH]At the signing of the Compact, Agares bound Abaddon in a pit beneath the Underhome. In later ages the dwarven city of Vallum is built atop this pit and the Vigil of the Deep and the Umberguard was established to make sure Abbadon is never released. [PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Ruin Belphegor shall send Oriens heads to the underground city of Vallum to free Abbadon, but the Vigil of the Deep catches and the Keeper of Keys executes Oriens before he can do so.
Belphegor the Daystar

[TAB]Though many mark the start of the Age of Ruin at the birth of Belphegor, it is more proper to date it from the earlier instant when Gosea the Dwindling escaped from hell and entered creation. [PARAGRAPH]The trauma of passing from hell to creation, and the thousands of demons she hosted, left her exhausted and comatose in the Fane of Lessers. She is found by the Knights of Judicium who bring her to Judicium. [PARAGRAPH]The inquisitors of Judicium know that Gosea is demon possessed and attempt to constrain her, but are no match for the thousands of demons that possess her. She slaughters the knights, takes control of Judicium, and frees the thousands of demons that are trapped there. [PARAGRAPH]Deep beneath the prison the Lorum Diaboli is guarded by Nera, an Aspect of Law, in the form of a Shield Dragon. He fights for decades against the demonic hordes that attempt to get the Lorum Diaboli, and he never falls. [PARAGRAPH]The prison also contains the Crucible. Realizing its power Gosea orders the freed demonic spirits to:[PARAGRAPH]"Go to every corner of creation. Inhabit every willing host and whisper to them the secrets of dark magic and the names of the old gods. On Samhain I will stop the Crucible and allow magic to flow once again into Erebus. Have your new witches and sorcerers prepare rituals for that night, and be ready for the new power we bring them. "[PARAGRAPH]And they did as she commanded. [PARAGRAPH:3]Bhall lies dying. Her faith is largely forgotten and her power in creation is limited. Sarabride holds the Heart of Fire, denying her creator access to its infinite reserves of fire. The Plains of Dust is a place of entropy and ruin, not healing. And every century she spends there brings her closer to death. Rather than allow her to die, Agares shares his power with her; this is in opposition to his dominion and it weakens both him and the role of Entropy in creation. [PARAGRAPH]Their union produces a child: Belphegor the Day Star. As the product of two gods, this demonic prince is more powerful than any archangel. He is the king of lust and perversion, and with his birth all manner of sexual depravity appears in Creation. [PARAGRAPH:2]Four specific demons released by Gosea conspire to bring Belphegor into Creation. They are true demons, normally too powerful to bother possessing a mortal, but their plan drives them. [PARAGRAPH]Lucian- A spirit of jealousy, inhabits Amaymon the Untouched (the beautiful, who Belphegor calls Melancholy). [PARAGRAPH]Alastor- A spirit of cruelty, inhabits Oriens the Pederast (the cruel and depraved). [PARAGRAPH]Acedia- A spirit of apathy, inhabits Egyn the Fleshmonger (to which many men gave their fortunes and more, as evidenced by his odd collection of foreskins). [PARAGRAPH]Saffa- A spirit of seduction, inhabits Egyn's wife Paymon Hora (who desires and is desired, and who is called the All Bride). [PARAGRAPH:2]The Summoning of Belphegor[PARAGRAPH]Amaymon, Oriens, Egan and Paymon go to Prespur of the Storms. There they build an elaborate summoning chamber for the ritual that is to come. The acts performed to merge the room with hell are vile even by the standards of the Calabim. [PARAGRAPH]Once the room is prepared Amaymon goes to a Calabim ball where her beauty draws the attention of Flauros. Flauros follows her back to the ritual chamber they have prepared, which was built to trap the vampire king. None of Flauros's desires are fulfilled; instead the four imprison him and summon the soul of Belphegor into him. [PARAGRAPH]Flauros resists the possession, but by the end his will is entirely subjugated by Belphegor; the demon prince makes Flauros's body his own. By the time the Calabim realize that Flauros is missing, Belphegor and his followers are gone. Alexis tasks Ravana's hunter clan and Stolas's sorcerer clan with finding him, but they are unsuccessful. [PARAGRAPH:2]When Belphegor seduces Sarabrid, fire rains down on creation and ash fills the sky. After succumbing, Sarabride goes to Yggdrasil. The forests around it are already on fire, but the world tree stands untouched. As Gwenhwyfar watches in horror, Sarabride uses the Heart of Fire to burn Yggdrasil to a ruined husk, closing the way to both the Infinite Garden and the Wildlands. Gwenhwyfar is killed attempting to defend Yggdrasil, though she will return as an angel of Cernunnos to stand watch over the burnt husk of the tree. [PARAGRAPH]Belphegor instructs all those that worship him to go release the Unraveling and destroy creation.

Salamanders are made for war. Most were crusaders in life, spending their days on blood-soaked battlefields in allegiance to some ideal or command. Now the illusions of their ideals have been stripped from them and war is all that they seek. Salamanders differ from Camulos's demons in that they seek war for the ability to inflict pain and the sheer chaos. Salamanders love war for the conflict, for the struggle, for the clash of ideologies (even if they don't care which ideology wins). Leaders of rebellions are fond of summoning salamanders to aid them.
Silkie

These spirits appear as beautiful women in white gowns. Arawn has denied them access to the Otherworld. Now they wander creation. They tend to appear to heroes that are close to death, though they rarely interfere. They hope that somehow they can pass with that hero into death. Seeing a Silkie is generally a bad omen. [PARAGRAPH]Some Silkies morn having never had children and will occasionally "adopt" a baby. They appear to the child as he grows, less so as he gets older and can help protect the child. Silkies are in Arawn's dominion, they are not undead, because their spirits are bound to creation by Arawn's curse, not a perversion of death magic.
Silkies are naturally immortal units that will abandon you if you leave the Eternal Cabal state religion
Maoliosa the Barren

Maoliosa formed the Elohim cult called "The Betrothed" who killed themselves in a ceremony to become the brides of Arawn. Maoliosa is a particularly evil woman who never believed that any of the other woman would become the brides of Arawn, but that they would be her gift to Arawn that would cause him to fall in love with her. Arawn was so offended by the gesture that he didn't allow any of the women to enter the Otherworld and now they wander creation as Silkies. The curse, and the centuries has made Maoliosa crueler and now she (usually accompanied by many Silkies) wanders creation attempting to cause as much death as possible in the mistaken belief that it will somehow curry Arawn's favor. [PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Invention Maoliosa submits to Auric Ulvin and she and her Silkies become the concubines of death (despite the protests of Laroth).
Neasa

Neasa was the youngest member (just over 12 years old) of "the Betrothed", a cult that killed themselves in an elaborate wedding ceremony to become the brides of Arawn. Arawn was so offended by the act that he didn't let any of them enter the Otherworld and they wander creation as Silkies instead. Neasa is the most friendly of the silkies, and will occasionally appear to those in need as a ghostly young girl in a white gown. She is likely to help those that are trying to avenge a murder. [PARAGRAPH]During the Age of Invention Neasa doesn't follow the rest of the Silkies to serve Auric, but stays in the Elohim city of Niveus instead, and is occasionally seen around the temple of the Matronae.
Merry Dancer

A Merry Dancer is a demon who has been saved by the compassion of Sirona. They have repented and forsaken all forms of violence and hatred and are now creatures of joy, beauty and peace. [PARAGRAPH]As angels of Sirona they continue to minister to those damned to hell, offering them the same forgiveness that allows them to repent become Merry Dancers themselves. [PARAGRAPH]Sallos was a soldier from a small and dismal duchy at the edge of the Patrian Empire. He grew tired of what he thought was a meaningless life. When he captured a Merry Dancer he sacrificed the creature in the hope that something will hear his call. His call was heard and Hyborem answered and offered him seven years of power in exchange for his eternal servitude and that of his descendants.

Merry Dancers are purely defensive and not particularly strong when it comes to combat, but they may the be best troops to use against the Infernal. Their special ability allows you convert your rival's demonic units into more Merry Dancers serving you.

Mithril is prized in part for its ability to resist spells of all kinds, leading to highly sought after armor for any warrior. However, even the Luchuirp Arch-Enchanters found themselves unable to bind any enchantments, no matter what form it was given. For a long time the idea was thought to be impossible. Then one day a dwarven city was overrun by a legion of drowned. The Artificer who found the ruins cried out to Nantosuelta, rending his clothes as he fell to his knees in horror. Every dwarven woman and child had been beheaded, the men dragged towards the waters, presumably to rise again and spread the misery further through the land. Nantosuelta's heart broke, and she spoke to the Artificer, instructing him to build the largest golem ever seen, shaped like a dwarf but cast of pure Mithril. When the time golem was finished, he was told, Nantosuelta would give it life as their spells could not. What they would do with it was up to them; the goddess knew she was intervening too much already. The Tinker nodded, and gathered his hammer and set off for the Holy city. It would take a long time to forge the parts, and much blood would be shed as he toiled stoically day after day. But the evil would be pushed from the land-forever.
Formed of mithril and infused with the power of Nantosuelta herself, the Mithril Golem is an avatar unit and one of the most powerful units in the game.
Khalida the Suicidal

Khalida is suicidal. She often kills herself, but her power brings her back, alive and full of even stronger death magic. She pays a horrible price for her power, but does it when she has no other option.

The Druids were priests of Sucellus since the Age of Dragons, when he lived among the Elves and presided over the dominion of Nature. They continue to honor him now that he has risen as the God of Life, but some of the Unblemished hold that most Druids are still too tainted by the dogmas of his original sphere to serve him properly in this age. The Reborn are the greatest healers in Erebus, often able to raise the long dead and almost always able to resurrect themselves indefinitely.

Genius

Amathaon does not have a hierarchy of priests and high priests. He does not bless his worshipers with miracles, but grants great talents to many individuals apparently at random. Those who worship Amathaon are no more likely to be gifted with such talents, but they work hard to help others develop their gifts. A Curator is focused on help Great Persons develop their full potential, although their is some chance that enough experience around the highly talented may help one become a Genius in his own right.

The Genius is the closest equivalent to a High Priest found among the House of Plenty, but unlike other high priests they are not upgraded from normal priests at level 6. Curators cannot become Geniuses, but any Great Person (that does not follow a different faith) may upgrade to a Genius and gain superior versions of the abilities of all the great person types.

The Dybbuk are malicious spirits that can control the soul of someone who recently died. They have little power over the just, though those burdened with sin are easy prey for them. The Dybbuk can force the soul to possess a living or dead host. [PARAGRAPH]Ghoul- When a Dybbuk leaves a corrupted soul in the body of a dead host it becomes a ghoul. [PARAGRAPH]Wight- When a Dybbuk leaves a corrupted soul in the body of a dead host and the Dybbuk remains to strengthen and control the soul then the creature is known as a Wight. Wights are more powerful than ghouls and their touch steals the life and strength of their victim. Although Dybbuk prefer to not draw too much attention to themselves when threatened they can usually raise a group of ghouls lead by a Wight to defend themselves

A Dybbuk with access to Sluaghs (whose alignments are not Good) can use them possess and take control of living units or undead units. The undead units gain all the promotions from the Sluagh. The Sluagh is used up in the process, preventing future resurrections

Dreamer

I have not been able to discern how the Cultists choose their Dreamers. Sometimes it is a vagrant, sometimes the son or daughter of a noble, and everyone in between seems eligible. He is abducted and taken to temple, usually on the night of the full moon. The hands and feet are bound. Sleep is induced. Some sects use various herbal concoctions; this one simply strangled the man until he passed out. He is laid in a shallow pool, submerged partially in sea water.[PARAGRAPH:1]All night the Cultists gather around, listening for anything he might say in this sleep. This becomes the Dreamer's new name. It is etched onto a clay jar, which is filled with sea water. I observed the names on some of these. "The Leviathan Trembles But Does Not Awaken," read one. "Pour the Blood of the Slaves Into the Styx," another. The victim tonight seemed to hear nothing, for he was silent as he slept, nearly until dawn. Should this be the case, the victim is drowned and serves in the undead army of the Undertow. Fortunately for this man, or perhaps not, he at last called out screaming, "The distant one has watching eyes!"[PARAGRAPH:1]The Cultists nodded to each other and pulled the man from the water. When he saw them holding him, he cringed. They spoke not to him, but dragged him to the back of the temple. I was unable to follow, but observed the Dreamer days later in sea colored robes. He had bloodshot eyes, and moved through the crowd in the town marketplace engaged in a constant dialogue with himself.[PARAGRAPH:2]From chapter 7 of Reflections on the State Cults, by Elder Methyl of the Luonnotar.

Kraken are a rare but terrifying sight for any sailor, and a potent weapon when commanded by an Undertow priest. Even in death, their bodies contain potent magics and can be used in a variety of minor spells. The massive eyes are especially useful, able to be enchanted to give a priest vision of a large area nearby.

The galley was the first ship designed for war. Galleys were powered by banks of oars on each side, manned by well-trained oarsmen. These oarsmen were highly paid professionals or patriotic citizens (except in Undertow countries). A huge, bronze "beak" mounted at the bow of the ship was used to ram and sink enemy ships. Because of its long, narrow hull, the galley was very unstable in all but the calmest waters, and as a consequence its crew rarely ventured out of sight of land for long periods of time, lest the ship be caught in a storm and sunk.

They called him an affective dreamer. It was a horrible attunement with magic that few were cursed with; what he dreamed became real.[PARAGRAPH:1]When he was 12, Hemah saw salamanders playing on the wet stones. They were like living pieces of painted mercury, tiny dragons who had an entire primordial world underneath the dock behind his home. They hissed at Hemah, as if confidence alone would keep him from squashing them.[PARAGRAPH:1]That night the hisses came again, but lower, echoing through the small stone house. Slick painted demons broke through the walls. With forked tongues, they scuttled through the shadows and grabbed Hemah's parents, dragging them from the house.[PARAGRAPH:1]He slept through it all. In the morning, the neighbors' screams woke him. Most of the house had collapsed, only his room remained standing. The neighbor's wife was a round woman with a voice so high she seemed to squeal like the pigs she and her husband raised. She rushed in and threw herself on Hemah, checking to make sure he was okay. They told him to close his eyes before they led him out of his room, but he looked.[PARAGRAPH:1]Claw marks, blood, everything was broken...and his parents were missing. They searched everywhere for them, but couldn't find them, but Hemah knew where they were. He led the pig farmer and his wife to the river behind their home and looked beneath the dock. That's where they found Hemah's parents' broken bodies, their mouths stuffed with so much mud their throats had exploded.[PARAGRAPH:1]Since then, everyone who has gotten close to Hemah has died, not that those who don't know him do much better. One morning, he awoke to find the entire population of the small village he was passing through was simply gone. Sometimes creatures are created that live well after he awakes. People are killed, women are raped. Men are made into puppets for the night, forced to play out scenes from Hemah's subconscious over and over again.[PARAGRAPH:1]Some say Hemah isn't a mage, he only dreamt he was once and he hasn't forgotten the dream. Others wonder if the Undertow found Hemah and caused his dreams, or if Hemah dreamt of the Undertow and created them. What is known is that as dangerous as Hemah is awake, he is even more dangerous asleep.
Hemah is an excellent spell caster available to Undertow followers only. His Channeling I-IV promotions and two affinities (Water and Mind) make him one of the greatest caster's in the game

The old captain reluctantly rose from his seat at the cabin, where he had been perusing his collection of maps. They had arrived, one of the crew had told him in a rather shaken voice. He was not at all comfortable with the situation, but he knew that he must not show it, or even think of it. They could sense that kind of thing, he had heard, and while not superstitious, he nevertheless was a careful man, the evidence of which being the fact that he had managed to become so old despite his dangerous profession.[PARAGRAPH:1]As he came up on deck, he noticed that the afternoon sun had given way to foggy twilight. He must have been in the cabin for longer than he thought, though a small voice in the back of his mind told him that it was because of their presence. He resolved to ignore the voice, but he feared it was going to become more insistent soon. He'd better get these negotiations over with quickly, hopefully he would receive the reward without trouble, and be able to head home to Selena as soon as possible. The small voice laughed at this thought, but it was a bitter and humorless laughter tinged with desperation.[PARAGRAPH:1]He saw their ship anchored next to theirs, he saw the plank that had provided a makeshift bridge, and finally his eyes fell upon the dark silhouette standing on the deck before him, with a few smaller ones scattered behind.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Good evening, captain. It is truly a nice ship you've got here."[PARAGRAPH:1]The voice was warm and friendly in a slightly disturbing sort of way, a little bit like the warm and friendly voice of a predator luring its prey, the small voice commented. The figure made a gesture with what the captain fervently hoped was its arm, apparently meant simply to indicate the ship, but somehow managing to appear much more ominous. By the Undertow, this was unsettling! Then, a bit too late to be proper etiquette, he realized that he was expected to say something.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Y-yes, thank you. Reputedly the best ship in the fleet, we are...."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Of course you are. We chose you for the mission. Because your ship was chosen by Us, it follows logically that it is the best. We do not make mistakes. Thus it is and thus it always will be. Tell us of your mission."[PARAGRAPH:1]The captain was momentarily baffled at the way the tone of voice so quickly changed from alluring to commanding, but he could do nothing but obey. In a voice more stuttering in actuality than the captain believed it to be, he recounted the story of the past week. Of how they had sailed with the rest of the fleet to lead the final attack. Of how the fleet had sailed through hidden canals and shallow rivers to take the city by surprise. Of how the captain and his crew had, the night before the fleet reached the city, stealthily left the fleet to sail ahead and warn the city of the attack, betraying the positions of the other ships. Of how soldiers from the city had rushed to the ships' position under cover of darkness, destroying them and massacring their unprepared crews with ease.[PARAGRAPH:1]As the tale progressed, the captain felt increasingly uncomfortable, and it must have been evident on his face, because the dark figure replied:[PARAGRAPH:1]"Do not trouble yourself with meaningless guilt, captain. When We first approached you, We offered you a choice between death and life. You chose life. Life at the expense of many deaths, deaths of friends and allies perhaps, but life nonetheless. It was the rational choice. It is the choice We would have made. Given the circumstances, yes, it was the right choice. You couldn't have known, after all..."[PARAGRAPH:1]The captain at first felt comforted by this, but then he suddenly heard the last sentence again in his mind, and a great feeling of horror overcame him.[PARAGRAPH:1]"No...no...please...no..."he moaned[PARAGRAPH:1]"You did not know that the choice We offered to you was not in fact a choice between life and death, but rather a choice between loyalty and betrayal. What We knew and you did not was that death would follow in either case. As We previously said, We do not make mistakes. Letting you live would be a mistake."[PARAGRAPH:1]"No...NO! You promised...you promised...what have I done...?" The captain was sobbing now. [PARAGRAPH:1]"An amusing comment. A betrayer should know better than to hold others to their word, We find."[PARAGRAPH:1]The dark figure took a staff that had been hanging on its back, and proceeded to ram it straight downwards into the ship, ignoring the sobbing captain. A flash of darkish purple light shone, and when the captain looked up again through his tear-filled eyes, They had vanished, along with their ship, leaving an enormous hole straight through the vessel, which was quickly starting to take in water. As the rest of the crew rushed about on the ship, panicking and making feeble attempts at saving themselves, the captain merely sat on his knees in front of the crack, thinking of the lives he had destroyed, thinking of Selena, thinking of his folly, all the while longing for the waves that would end his suffering.[PARAGRAPH:1]As They knew then, and he did not, the suffering of him and his crew was not, in fact, about to end. It was about to begin.

The Doviello carry crude weapons into battle, a throwing rock bigger than a man's head or a stout branch. They use these makeshift weapons because they were temporary. The first opponent killed becomes their weapon of choice. Grabbed by the ankles, they would be swung like a meaty flail. Blood sprayed over opponents, and every swing would lose more and more of the corpse, until another was needed to replace the first. At this point in the battle, the "weapons" were always readily available. Occasionally, an opponent would be grabbed while still alive. The effect of being beaten by a bloody body that was screaming at you while it happened is traumatizing to even the most hardened warrior. Few armies were willing to face even a few hundred Doviello.[PARAGRAPH:1]Saverous was a Doviello warrior, captured by the Burnt Priest and transported to an asylum where he could be the subject of experiments. He would have died there, or worse, gone months without death, but a war began. The Undertow searched their slaves for useful bodies, warriors were sacrificed, priests were pulled from their work to fight. Saverous was nearly 9 feet tall, his body still strong, even if his mind was broken from the experiments. They made him into a thrull.[PARAGRAPH:1]Possessed by a demon and inscribed with runes that hardened his skin and strengthened his muscles, Saverous was loosed on the battlefield, and Arawn help any man who stood in his way.
Saverous will only join Undertow civilizations. Saverous is a powerful warrior with a high strength and a built in bonus against melee troops; he frequently leads the Undertow into battle.

Perhaps our late queen was not as foolish as I thought when she built that accursed gate. Although I am loathe to admit it, I am glad that I had Basium fight beside me in this war. I am even more glad to see his Mercurians leave this world behind. I would never welcome them back into the land of the living, and their brutal tactics are not what I would choose to use against even the most depraved denizens of hell, but they have been of service. I doubt we could have reclaimed this realm without them. To conquer, however, is not the same as to restore. There is still much work to do in service of our true purpose. As we have done since the time of Immanuel, we must rebuild the world through love. There are orphans to shelter, widows to console, and a whole world full of imperfect beings to lead towards enlightenment.
The time of my life is over, but my ministry is just begun. The prisoners of the great machine of hell, and even its wardens, must be shown the forgiveness that Sirona offers.

The people called for war. I called for peace; I was mistaken. It seems now that our truce with these devils was a terrible folly, which has cost the world dearly. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]War came despite our best efforts, and when it did we were ill prepared. Things would be so different had we acted sooner. The Queen might never have seen a need to betray our ancient traditions and used our secret lore build that accursed gate. The Mercurian hordes would never have been unleashed to "defend" Erebus by laying waste to it. Ethne, and so many others, would still be alive. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]We should have come here long ago, to halt the encroachment of hell upon the lands of the living before they could threaten those we were sworn to protect. . . those I was sworn to protect. Oh, how I have failed them! Even my own wife is lost, by my own hand. I cannot avenge the dark deed that made this murder a mercy, but perhaps can prevent such abominations from ever happening again. If not. . . well, maybe this hellscape is the only afterlife I deserve. I can only pray that the wisdom of Sirona keep me from corruption, and turn my fate into a ministry to the damned.

Hawks, Ravens, and Parrots are air domain units that may not move around the map like normal land or sea units, but may be moved directly from one city to another or carried by various recon units. They can be used to get a bird's eye view of the land, revealing tiles as well and seeing through the invisibility of various units. In a normal game, you can build these instead of capturing them.
Because of their rarity gorillas are among the most difficult animal to capture on most maps. They tend to appear in jungles, though even then you are unlikely to find large groups.
Because of their rarity baboons are among the most difficult animal to capture on most maps. They tend to appear in jungles, though even then you are unlikely to find large groups.

Panthers are dangerous hunters and very capable of taking out a lone scout or unguarded settler. There is more to fear in the jungles than just the lizardmen. Panthers start with the Woodsman I and Stealth promotion, so they are stronger in jungle tiles and can be very difficult to see.

I am the last warrior of the Godswar. For others it ended ages ago, but I must see it to the end. I sacrificed my place by my god's side lest I be bound by that old accord to stop my sacred duty. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The good gods were fools to sign The Compact while our side was winning, rather than extinguish evil while we had the chance. The neutral gods were cowards and traitors for demanding a ceasefire rather than joining the stronger side to end the conflict once and for all. I am ashamed to say that my own maker was among these cowards, and my sister fully supported him. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Over the past few ages the tide has turned. The conflict remains, but is buried beneath the surface. The gods now use men as pawns in their game, which would be fine if the rules of the game were not so biased towards the other side. Erebus has reached a point of crisis like it has never seen before, yet everyone seems to ignore it. I cannot ignore it. The world would fall into hellfire without me. Os-Gabella (always the pawn of Ceridwen) means to end the world entirely, and is using Hyborem as a tool to do it. Somehow they have tricked two other nations into helping them, although even the most wicked mortals should be wise enough to know that this cannot be in their interests. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I would fight them all alone if need be, but fortunately I have found some allies as well. The Queen of the Elohim Nation has realized the folly of her ancestors' peaceful ways, and used their most secret lore to build a gate to summon my army to the place were we are most needed. A priest of Lugus has organized a council of good nations to stand against its darker rival. It is still dominated by pacifist fools, but may serve as a useful tool regardless. A group of elves still loyal to the precept of nature has joined his confederation in an attempt to gain an upper hand in their feud with their more mischievous brethren, and now find themselves relying on it to defend themselves from an all out Infernal invasion. As they serve Cernunnos now instead of Sucellus, the might not be completely useless.

With the long winter ended, the ancient Civil War rages again. It has now grown in scope and and spilled over into lands far beyond the Umbrawood, involving peoples who neither know nor care about its cause. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Svartalfar established a council of those who walk in darkness, and used it to draw in allies against us. Perhaps we could stand along against both our darker brothers and the Calabim, but in their fervor to destroy us they have done the unthinkable and chosen to help the Sheaim in their quest to destroy the whole world. The Seelie Court has fled our sacred capital of Evermore, as Faeryl's assassins have been picking us off one by one and it seems inevitable that her armies will seize the whole city soon. This however seems a small matter compared to the corruption that began at Tempus Mor and now spreads towards our heartland. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In the face of catastrophe I begged for aid from the Elohim, an ancient nation of righteous men much beloved by Sucellus. Their Queen has invited us to join the Overcouncil, a confederation founded by a holy man living with the nomads far away in Desert of Myrh. It was a great surprise when I found this holy man to in fact be an elf, and a very strange one. His wife was a druid trained in my own court, yet he knew very little of our ways or of this ancient conflict. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In the ancient tongue of men he told me a tale of how his father had been a mercenary serving an archmage during the fall of Patria. This wicked sorcerer took Arak the Erkling, his young sons, and his army with him as he fled from Kylorin by invading the land of the dead. The Once Elves were still his prisoners in the Otherworld when Faeryl betrayed me. In time they would escape, but chose to settle in the darkness of the rift between worlds rather than rejoin the elven nation. He grew up as the ward of his elder brother, King Haerlond, an unprincipled pragmatist with poor tastes in advisors. When a group of children wandered into Barathrum and uncovered their necromancer's plot against the innocent Talia, he risked his life in service of the truth. When the Shadowed Vale fell, he was given a vision of Lugus which led him settle among the Malakim. He claims to have since then found enlightenment in the Mirror of Heaven, and rarely ceases preaching his gospel to all who will hear it. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He seemed disappointed that we were not willing to abandon our ancient religion for his new cult, yet he did not force the matter. We were welcomed into the alliance regardless. While for the moment the Malakim are unable to devote an army to defend Evermore, he has pledged to aid us by occupying the Svartalfar on another front. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]On our journey back to Dendrom, the world was shaken and forever changed. The corruption that gripped the edges of the Umbrawood gave way to darker terrain, as Erebus began to merge with hell itself. The Sheaim's schemes were coming to fruition. The children of Sucellus are to be destroyed by Agares' dark imitation of our god. The abomination that the Black Mirror conjured when Cernunnos invaded hell to rescue Gower has come to Erebus and captured Yonna. Our party barely survived our first encounter with the Infernal. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ethne has been a true blessing. We could not have survived had she not sent medics from The Unblemished to tend to our wounded. She has sent her own troops into harm's way on our behalf several times, and usually paid dearly. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Recently the sight of so much suffering has moved her to take an unprecedented action. She has defied the Elohim law to summon the archangel Basium to come to our aid. Although our elder priests are upset that he blasphemes the name of Sucellus (his rightful lord), we know he is our greatest hope for vanquishing the Infernal from our homeland.

With the long winter ended, the ancient Civil War rages again. At last I shall be able to topple that "beloved queen" Arendel and claim the summer throne for my own. Towards this goal I established the Undercouncil. I of course realize that these new allies will cause problems of their own later on, but my hatred of Phaedra is enough to risk them that for the time being. Is it not better to keep such peoples as the Sheaim as close friends, even with diametrically opposed goals? What is a friend anyway but the best kind of enemy, an enemy who will not defend himself because he does not yet realize that you are at war?

We warred for eons in the deepest hell, proud of the kingdoms we forged but knowing their futility. I have been called the greatest of archangels, the darker half of one who became a god, and yet even my domain in Nyx shall surely pass away some day and be replaced chiefdoms of mortal souls who have yet to be refined. Since the Queen of Passion has joined us and awakened, we all have come to yearn for world beyonds our own. Creation is the goal of many, but Erebus must be made my footstool alone. The Twenty-One have made this difficult, but not impossible. This world may not bend easily to my will, but many mortals do. For years we have made deals and traded secrets to shortsighted mortals to prepare ourselves a way. Within a few generations, the armies amassing in the Fane of the Lessers will be free to overrun all but the most holy of lands. I could have waited, but instead chose to take a shortcut provided by a suicidal immortal. I come now invited to this world, treading carefully lest I violate any clause of that old arrangement to which the King of Hope must hold me hostage.
